title: Contrasts keep framing and scale
statement: When a picture contrasts two states, keep the framing and scale identical in both halves so that only the contrast changes.
detail: Two version-3 inference lesson designs for a Grade 3 course ask for a wide illustration split into two contrasting halves of the same story or moment, with identical framing and scale on both so the contrast reads instantly (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Instruction/3.1 - Fantasy Classics - Lesson Designs/3.1 - 2. Aladdin and the Wonderful Lamp, Part 2 (FICTION, INFER) — v3 (new INFER design).docx`, line 60 of its text; `downloads/5. Curriculum/Instruction/3.1 - Fantasy Classics - Lesson Designs/3.1 - 9. The Wind in the Willows, Part 2 (FICTION, INFER) — v3 (new INFER design).docx`, line 58). The picture carries the lesson's main idea before the child reads (the first design, line 56). No outcome was measured.

evidence.path: 5. Curriculum/Instruction/3.1 - Fantasy Classics - Lesson Designs/3.1 - 2. Aladdin and the Wonderful Lamp, Part 2 (FICTION, INFER) — v3 (new INFER design).docx
evidence.quote: Identical framing and scale on both halves so the contrast in the boy's power reads instantly
